> The Mini Robotic Arm is a custom-designed, 3D-printed robotic arm created using Fusion360, featuring five servo motors to control its base, 2 arm joints, gripper rotation, and gripping mechanism. It is controlled by an Aruduino Uno Rev3 CH340, with two analog joysticks for precise manual movement and two push buttons to open and close the gripper. The project combines mechanical design, electronics, and embedded programming to create a functional robotic system. Through this project, I aim to develop my skills in CAD modelling robotics and hardware integration. (Robotic Arm inspired by Tony Stark too)

## Design

### 2026-10-12 – Before anything, even before the week started, I immediately went on and search for projects, searching through Atlantis, common project ideas that other student make online and all. Some of these ide

**2h**

Before anything, even before the week started, I immediately went on and search for projects, searching through Atlantis, common project ideas that other student make online and all. Some of these ideas would be a land rover, a rocket that can fly and safely come back down, a pinball machine, and a robotic arm. All of these are without the inclusion of the marble race that I also wanted to automate it using a DC motor. Finding a project, in my opinion was one of the hardest thing, then I found inspiration for the robotic arm project and decided that will be the project that I will do.

Hence, I went to design the entire project through sketches and create the BOM, it took me a whole hour and 30 minutes, with the other 30 minutes used on sketching through ideas. I just know that the hardest part of this entire CAD designing would be the firmware part for the controls of the robotic arm.

Well, I got my project, I got my BOM, I got my ideas, and now, it's time to launch and do the entire thing!

### 2026-10-14 – In order for the entire arm to actually work, there are firmware that needs to be added into it to allow the controls to control the entire robotic arm. In order to do that, I went on wokwi.com to bui

**2.75h**

In order for the entire arm to actually work, there are firmware that needs to be added into it to allow the controls to control the entire robotic arm. In order to do that, I went on wokwi.com to build a small simulation of the entire robotic arm, with 5 servo motors, an Arduino Uno as the main MCU, 2 analog Joysticks and 2 push buttons, exactly the same way that it will be connected in my CAD file. The entire code and building of that thing took 2 hours, with most of the time spending on the firmware to make it run, debugging code issues, and requiring sketching and practical examples of how it will work with the joysticks and the buttons.

That's mostly it for this session, the firmware will also be uploaded to Github.
